selected_evidence.requirement: Automatic unlock and mount at boot
selected_evidence.summary: Shows generated cryptsetup and mount units plus boot-journal proof that systemd unlocked and mounted the volume automatically.
Captures the healthy baseline boot ID, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and recovered encrypted volume with preserved data and zero failed units.

commands.command:
set -eu
install -d -m 0700 /etc/cryptsetup-keys.d
install -d -m 0700 /var/lib/secure-volume
if [ ! -e /etc/cryptsetup-keys.d/secure.key ]; then dd if=/dev/urandom of=/etc/cryptsetup-keys.d/secure.key bs=64 count=1 status=none; fi
chmod 0600 /etc/cryptsetup-keys.d/secure.key
if [ ! -e /var/lib/secure-volume/secure.luks ]; then fallocate -l 512M /var/lib/secure-volume/secure.luks; fi
stat -c 'key mode=%a owner=%U:%G size=%s' /etc/cryptsetup-keys.d/secure.key
stat -c 'container mode=%a owner=%U:%G size=%s' /var/lib/secure-volume/secure.luks

stat -c 'mount-root mode=%a owner=%U:%G' /srv/secure
